body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_k=\sum_{g\in E_k}N_k^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_g}(Y_{i,g+k}-\widehat m^0_{i,g+k}),\quad \mathcal C_{n,k}=[\widehat\tau_k\pm c_{1-\alpha,n}\widehat s_k]\)

sampling_model.design: Deterministic absorbing staggered adoption with the untreated cells missing by a nested staircase after each unit's adoption date.
sampling_model.units: The primary domain is a complete triangular array in the note-specific event-transfer class: deterministic exact-rank factor means, blockwise uniform geometry, independent centered row-heteroskedastic sub-Gaussian errors, variance replication, and log-power-five cell leverage.  The separately defined published Choi--Yuan class permits \(M^0=M^\star+M^R\), uses global geometry and i.i.d. homoskedastic noise, and is incomparable with the event-transfer class.
sampling_model.treatment: The causal effect is added after \(G_i\); the target averages eligible treated units with unit-share rather than equal-cohort weights.
sampling_model.overlap: Every eligible cohort-horizon block has donor-row and pre-period Gram eigenvalues bounded uniformly away from zero after size normalization.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The feasible protocol still uses blockwise Choi--Yuan completion and debiasing, leave-one-cell-out untreated residuals, unit variance estimates, plug-in influence coefficients, and Gaussian multipliers.  Oracle variance concentration is proved, whereas the nonlinear remainder is represented by \(\mathcal R_n(u)\) and the normalized score-loading discrepancy by \(\mathcal B_n(h)\); their stochastic rates are not supplied by the class definition.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The published model permits approximate rank, uses global geometry and i.i.d. homoskedastic noise, and its staggered Theorem 3.2 gives scalar-functional inference under six hypotheses.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The event-transfer class is proved incomparable, Proposition A.4 supplies only the source-submodel block specialization, and the common subclass is reserved for a transferable converse.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2.1 gives a fourth-root Gaussian approximation error with log power five for independent high-dimensional sums without covariance-matrix nonsingularity.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The generic remainder-event transfer verifies its variance, fourth-moment, and sub-exponential envelope conditions for the sign-expanded event score.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Event-time aggregation crosses calendar times and right factors, so its normal approximation and variance may differ from calendar-time inference.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The exact eventwise score and staircase covariance are combined with a generic finite-error transfer whose feasible coverage remains conditional on displayed diagnostics.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The multiplier bootstrap yields asymptotically valid simultaneous inference for staggered group-time treatment effects under conditional parallel trends.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The replacement theorem is a finite-error generic remainder-event analogue under low-rank MNAR completion, not unconditional feasible coverage.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The data-driven intervals estimate each missing panel entry and match an instance-wise Bayesian Cramer--Rao lower bound.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present result uses entrywise expansion as input and makes no efficiency or attainable-remainder claim.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The preprint gives heteroskedastic pointwise and nonasymptotic intervals for individual effects and scalar weighted bilinear functionals under staggered adoption.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The covariance theorem exposes the additional growing rowwise score-loading control needed for a whole event curve.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Gaussian anti-concentration permits honest multiplier confidence bands without a fixed extreme-value limit.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The generic theorem applies anti-concentration to the explicit remainder and score-stability perturbations.

body.tldr: The note now separates a note-specific event-transfer class from the incomparable published Choi--Yuan approximate-rank scalar-functional class.  The main finite-error result is a generic remainder-event transfer: the sign-expanded event score satisfies the Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato--Koike 2022 fourth-root Gaussian bound under log power five, while nonlinear remainder and feasible-score errors remain explicit event probabilities.  Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4 supplies only the specialization \(u=C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\) on \(\mathcal A_n(C)\), with its unsimplified blockwise union bound.  Growing-curve coverage remains conditional, and the attainable common-subclass converse remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published Choi--Yuan inference permits approximate rank but is organized around global geometry, i.i.d. homoskedastic noise, and one scalar group-at-time functional under six hypotheses.  It does not provide a simultaneous growing-block probability or the rowwise feasible-score rate for this event curve.  Generic high-dimensional Gaussian approximation controls the linear score but cannot create those panel-specific controls.
project_justification.niche: The useful object is a generic remainder-event transfer for the exact primitive-cell event score, followed by an honest Choi--Yuan specialization.  This separates universal Gaussian approximation from estimator-specific block remainders and makes class scope auditable.
project_justification.fill: The note proves exact eligible-unit aggregation and full staircase covariance, verifies the 2022 Gaussian theorem with \(B_n=C\sqrt mL_n(K)\), unit coordinate variances, fourth moments bounded by \(CmL_n(K)^2\), and a \(\psi_1\) envelope, and obtains error \(C\{L_n(K)^2\log^5((p\vee3)m)\}^{1/4}\).  The finite coverage map adds \(P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u)^c\}\), score-event failure, anti-concentration, and covariance-stability terms.  Proposition A.4 is then used only through \(\mathcal A_n(C)\subseteq\mathcal R_n(C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\).

body.related_work: Choi and Yuan, \cite{ChoiYuan2024MNAR}, allow \(M^0=M^\star+M^R\), impose global singular-vector geometry and i.i.d. homoskedastic sub-Gaussian noise, and state staggered Theorem 3.2 for a scalar group-at-time functional under six hypotheses.  Their supplementary Proposition A.4 gives a one-block entrywise expansion; aggregation over the growing eligible block family yields only the unsimplified finite union bound used here.  Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, Kato, and Koike, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKatoKoike2022Improved}, Theorem 2.1, provide the singular-covariance-safe fourth-root Gaussian approximation with log power five used for the linear event score.  The 2023 log-cubed result is not used because its covariance nondegeneracy is unavailable for a staircase correlation matrix.  Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2013Maxima}, Lemma 3.1, supply the singular-safe Gaussian comparison, and \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2014Bands} supplies anti-concentration.  Choi, Kwon, and Liao, \cite{ChoiKwonLiao2024Completion}, analyze fixed functionals rather than the frozen growing rowwise score error.  Ben-Michael and Feller, \cite{BenMichaelFeller2026Discussion}, motivate the right-to-carry event curve; Callaway and Sant'Anna, \cite{CallawaySantAnna2021DID}, obtain simultaneous staggered paths under parallel trends rather than this low-rank MNAR transfer.
body.interpretation: For a right-to-carry event curve, researchers may choose a deterministic diagnostic threshold \(u_n\), verify a simultaneous remainder event \(\mathcal R_n(u_n)\), and combine it with the score-stability diagnostic.  The common critical value is honest when the explicit finite-error terms vanish.  Using the published Choi--Yuan ratios sets \(u_n=C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\) only on the joint block event; the paper does not claim that event is uniformly likely.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The updated linear approximation now needs \(L_n(K)^2\log^5((p\vee3)m)\to0\), with balanced-loading elbow \(\log(Km)=o(m^{1/5})\).  The unresolved limitations are estimator-specific: no frozen premise makes the growing Choi--Yuan block union probability vanish or controls the feasible rowwise score discrepancy.  The published approximate-rank class also introduces an \(M^R\) bias absent from the event-transfer expansion, so upper-band validity does not transfer to that full class.  Finally, the KKT-level second-order map needed to test attainment of \(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\) is not present in the frozen primitives.
body.honest_scope: The delivered theorem is a generic finite-error transfer on the baseline event-transfer class, not unconditional feasible growing-curve coverage.  It permits singular staircase correlation and uses the log-power-five 2022 Gaussian approximation.  Asymptotic \(1-\alpha\) coverage is asserted only along arrays for which \(P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u_n)^c\}\to0\), \(P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0\), \(u_n\sqrt{\log(2p)}\to0\), and \(h_n\log^2(2p)\to0\).  Choi--Yuan supplies a blockwise specialization, not those probability limits.  The event-transfer and published classes are incomparable; a future converse must be built in their common exact-rank rank-one subclass, and approximate-rank upper validity needs a separate bias remainder.
